source_text: Praesente bis et Claudiano consulibus, XVI kalendas Augustas, Karthagine in secretario inpositis Sperato, Nartzalo et Cittino, Donata, Secunda, Vestia, Saturninus proconsul dixit: Potestis indulgentiam domini nostri imperatoris promereri, si ad bonam mentem redeatis. Speratus dixit: Numquam malefecimus, iniquitati nullam operam praebuimus; numquam malediximus, sed male accepti gratias egimus, propter quod imperatorem nostrum obseruamus. Saturninus proconsul dixit: Et nos religiosi sumus, et simplex est religio nostra, et iuramus per genium domini nostri imperatoris et pro salute eius supplicamus; quod et uos quoque facere debetis. Speratus dixit: Si tranquillas praebueris aures tuas, dico mysterium simplicitatis. Saturninus proconsul dixit: Initianti tibi mala de sacris nostris aures non praebebo; sed potius iurate per genium domini nostri imperatoris. Speratus dixit: Ego imperium huius saeculi non cognosco, sed magis illi deo seruio, quem nemo hominum uidit nec uidere his oculis potest. Furtum non feci; sed si quid emero, theloneum reddo, quia cognosco dominum meum et imperatorem regum omnium gentium. Saturninus proconsul dixit ceteris: Desinite huius esse persuasionis. Speratus dixit: Mala est persuasio homicidium facere, falsum testimonium dicere. Saturninus proconsul dixit: Nolite huius dementiae esse participes. Cittinus dixit: Nos non habemus alium quem timeamus, nisi dominum deum nostrum qui est in caelis. Donata dixit: Honorem Caesari quasi Caesari, timorem autem deo. Vestia dixit: Christiana sum. Secunda dixit: Quod sum, ipsud uolo esse. Saturninus proconsul Sperato dixit: Perseueras Christianus? Speratus dixit: Christianus sum. Et cum eo omnes consenserunt. Saturninus proconsul dixit: Numquid ad deliberandum spatium uultis? Speratus dixit: In re tam iusta nulla est deliberatio. Saturninus proconsul dixit: Quae sunt res in capsa uestra? Speratus dixit: Libri et epistulae Pauli uiri iusti. Saturninus proconsul dixit: Moram XXX dierum habete et recordemini. Speratus iterum dixit: Christianus sum. Et cum eo omnes consenserunt. Saturninus proconsul decretum ex tabella recitauit: Speratum, Nartzalum, Cittinum, Donatam, Vestiam, Secundam et ceteros, ritu Christiano se uiuere confessos, quoniam oblata sibi facultate ad Romanorum morem redeundi obstinanter perseuerauerunt, gladio animaduerti placet. Speratus dixit: Deo gratias agimus. Nartzalus dixit: Hodie martyres in caelis sumus; deo gratias. Saturninus proconsul per praeconem dici iussit: Speratum, Nartzalum, Cittinum, Veturium, Felicem, Aquilinum, Laetantium, Ianuariam, Generosam, Vestiam, Donatam, Secundam duci iussi. Vniuersi dixerunt: Deo gratias. Et statim decollati sunt pro nomine Christi.
pass_a_gloss: When Praesens was consul for the second time and Claudianus [Gebhardt; Usener: Condianus] were consuls, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of August, at Carthage, in the chamber, Speratus, Nartzalus and Cittinus, Donata, Secunda, Vestia having been brought in, Saturninus the proconsul said: You can earn the indulgence of our lord the emperor if you return to a sound mind. Speratus said: We have never done evil, we have given no effort to iniquity; we have never cursed, but when badly received we gave thanks, for which reason we observe our emperor. Saturninus the proconsul said: We also are religious, and our religion is simple, and we swear by the genius of our lord the emperor and make supplication for his health; which you also ought to do. Speratus said: If you will furnish your ears calm, I will speak the mystery of simplicity. Saturninus the proconsul said: To you beginning bad things about our sacred rites I will not furnish ears; but rather swear by the genius of our lord the emperor. Speratus said: I do not know the empire of this age, but rather I serve that God whom no man has seen nor can see with these eyes. I have not made theft; but if I shall have bought anything, I pay the toll, because I know my lord and the emperor of the kings of all nations. Saturninus the proconsul said to the rest: Cease to be of this persuasion. Speratus said: Evil is the persuasion to do homicide, to say false testimony. Saturninus the proconsul said: Do not be sharers of this madness. Cittinus said: We have no other whom we may fear, except the Lord our God who is in the heavens. Donata said: Honour to Caesar as to Caesar, but fear to God. Vestia said: I am Christian (fem.). Secunda said: What I am, that itself I want to be. Saturninus the proconsul said to Speratus: Do you persevere a Christian? Speratus said: I am a Christian. And all consented with him. Saturninus the proconsul said: Do you want a space for deliberating? Speratus said: In a matter so just there is no deliberation. Saturninus the proconsul said: What are the things in your box? Speratus said: Books and letters of Paul, a just man. Saturninus the proconsul said: Have a delay of thirty days and bethink yourselves. Speratus again said: I am a Christian. And all consented with him. Saturninus the proconsul recited the decree from the tablet: Speratus, Nartzalus, Cittinus, Donata, Vestia, Secunda and the rest, having confessed themselves to live by the Christian rite, since, the opportunity having been offered them of returning to the custom of the Romans, they have obstinately persevered, it pleases that they be punished by the sword. Speratus said: We give thanks to God. Nartzalus said: Today we are martyrs in the heavens; thanks to God. Saturninus the proconsul ordered it to be said through the herald: Speratus, Nartzalus, Cittinus, Veturius, Felix, Aquilinus, Laetantius, Ianuaria, Generosa, Vestia, Donata, Secunda I have ordered to be led away. All together said: Thanks to God. And immediately they were beheaded for the name of Christ.

choices.why: The copy-text prints Claudiano and the translation follows the lock. Gebhardt's apparatus gives Condiano (Usener), and the consuls of AD 180 are Praesens II and Condianus, so the printed form is likely scribal; that is stated in the translator note, not silently corrected in the text. A muse compare review failed source_identity on the earlier emended reading; the printed reading was restored on repair.
rejected: Condianus in the reading text (historically right, but not what the locked text says)

choices.why: Speratus answers a charge about the emperor by claiming observance of 'our emperor' — in context God (cf. section 6). Capital E marks the deliberate double sense without changing the words.
rejected: we obey the emperor (flattens the wordplay the scene turns on)

choices.why: ipsud is the old form of ipsum; Secunda's point is persistence in identity, matching Perseueras in section 10. 'Remain' keeps the martyrdom sense; lemma records the literal 'that itself I want to be'.
rejected: that itself I want to be (literal, kept in Pass A)

choices.english: they live by the Christian rite
choices.why: ritus is the legal charge word in the decree (a way/rite of life), not private belief; the sentence is a court formula and is kept formal.
rejected: they are Christians (loses the decree's legal wording)

bible_refs.note: Donata's 'Honorem Caesari quasi Caesari, timorem autem deo' reworks 'render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's'; Gebhardt's apparatus cites Mt 22:21 and Rom 13:7. Kept as possible allusion in notes only — the passio does not quote the verse, so no inline citation is forced.

variants: Section 1: Claudiano (text) / Condiano (Usener, apparatus). Section 6: JB reads 'dominum meum, regem regum et omnium gentium dominum'. Section 17: some witnesses add a reign clause after decollati sunt; not in Gebhardt's Latin column, not supplied.
pass_b_english: In the second consulship of Praesens, with Claudianus as his colleague, on 17 July, Speratus, Nartzalus, and Cittinus were brought into the hearing chamber at Carthage, and with them Donata, Secunda, and Vestia.

Saturninus the proconsul said: "You can earn the pardon of our lord the emperor if you come back to your right mind." Speratus said: "We have never done wrong. We have had no part in wickedness. We have never cursed anyone; when we were ill-treated, we gave thanks. That is why we revere our Emperor."
Saturninus the proconsul said: "We too are devout, and our religion is simple. We swear by the genius of our lord the emperor, and we pray for his well-being. You must do the same."
Speratus said: "If you will give me a quiet hearing, I will tell you the mystery of simplicity."
Saturninus the proconsul said: "I will not listen while you begin to speak evil of our sacred rites. Swear instead by the genius of our lord the emperor."

Speratus said: "I do not acknowledge the empire of this age. Rather, I serve that God, whom no human being has seen, or can see, with these eyes. I have never stolen. If I buy anything, I pay the tax, because I know my Lord and Emperor, the ruler of the kings of all nations."
Saturninus the proconsul said to the others: "Give up this persuasion of yours." Speratus said: "The evil persuasion is to commit murder and to bear false witness."
Saturninus the proconsul said: "Do not take part in this madness." Cittinus said: "We have no one else to fear, only the Lord our God, who is in heaven."
Donata said: "Honour to Caesar, as Caesar's due; but fear to God." Vestia said: "I am a Christian." Secunda said: "What I am, that I want to remain."
Saturninus the proconsul said to Speratus: "Do you persist in being a Christian?" Speratus said: "I am a Christian." And all the others agreed with him.
Saturninus the proconsul said: "Do you want time to think it over?" Speratus said: "In a cause so just, there is nothing to think over."
Saturninus the proconsul said: "What are the things in your case?" Speratus said: "Books, and letters of Paul, a righteous man."
Saturninus the proconsul said: "Take thirty days, and think it over." Speratus said again: "I am a Christian." And all the others agreed with him.

Saturninus the proconsul read the decree from the tablet: "Speratus, Nartzalus, Cittinus, Donata, Vestia, Secunda, and the rest have confessed that they live by the Christian rite. They were given the chance to return to the Roman way, and they obstinately held fast. It is therefore ordered that they be punished with the sword."
Speratus said: "We give thanks to God." Nartzalus said: "Today we are martyrs in heaven; thanks be to God."

Saturninus the proconsul ordered the herald to proclaim: "Speratus, Nartzalus, Cittinus, Veturius, Felix, Aquilinus, Laetantius, Ianuaria, Generosa, Vestia, Donata, and Secunda: I have ordered them to be led away."
All of them together said: "We give thanks to God." And at once they were beheaded for the name of Christ.
